# Draft:Dukla battlefield monuments

}}
The Dukla monuments are national cultural monuments dedicated to the Carpathian-Dukla Operation, which took place during World War II in the Dukla Pass area, and to the memory of the soldiers who died. The Dukla Operation took place in the pass through which the Soviet army came to the aid of the Slovak National Uprising. The monuments are located between Dukla and Svidník.
Monuments
Red Army Monument
In Svidník stands a monumental marble monument to the Red Army, a national cultural monument. It was unveiled on October 3, 1954 on the occasion of the celebration of the 10th anniversary of the Carpathian-Dukla operation. The authors of the project were Czech architects Karel Lodr, Jan Krumprecht and Václav Šedivý. The monument is 37 m high. The five-pointed star at its top measures 3.5 m. The front walls of the monument's enclosure artistically symbolize the Slovak National Uprising and the arrival of the Red Army.
